rejected.note: Fix the six blocking ones and the three defects a user can see: the wrong empty message on a load error, the stale customer filter, and the #12 search. The stricter email rule is what I want, hand-edited data is out of scope for this build, the clickable orders in the customer view and the shared DOM helpers go to a later slice, and the CI pin is a repo chore I will do myself.

confirmed.what_breaks: lineView.editingLineId is module-level state. Only a successful submit (line 106) and Cancel (line 85) reset it. The Back button (orders-view.js:136, show() at 17-21) does not. If the user clicks Edit on a line, then Back, then reopens the same order, the form opens as 'Edit line' with that line's values filled in, not as 'Add line'.
confirmed.evidence: Traced the path: buildRow Edit sets lineView.editingLineId = line.id (line 48). Back calls show(root, ctx, 'list'), which never touches lineView. When the order reopens, buildForm line 73 runs order.lines.find((l) => l.id === lineView.editingLineId), finds the line again and renders the edit form. No data is lost unless the user then saves over it, so this is advisory.

confirmed.what_breaks: The error banner is cleared only after a successful commit. A refusal stays on screen across tabs and screens and then sits above unrelated content, for example the 'This customer has 1 order...' refusal shown on the Orders tab.
confirmed.evidence: grep shows clearError() called only at app.js:60, inside commit() after a successful save. switchTab (65-68), orders-view show() (17-21) and the customer view navigation never call it. customers-view.js:113 calls ctx.showError(result.errors.orders) when a delete is refused. The message is correct when it first shows, so this is advisory.

confirmed.what_breaks: stateWith() always builds exactly one order (o1), so the tests cannot tell whether changeOrder writes lines only to the target order. A regression that wrote the new lines to every order would pass every lines test and corrupt the other orders.
confirmed.evidence: tests/lines.test.js:6-9 has orders: [order] only, and grep finds no 'o2' in the file. The current code at src/domain/lines.js:33 is correct, so this is a test gap and not a live defect.

confirmed.what_breaks: Every updateCustomer test (lines 68-89) uses stateWith([ana]) with a single customer. A regression that overwrote every customer with the edited fields would pass all R-03 tests.
confirmed.evidence: Read tests/customers.test.js:68-89: there is one customer in every updateCustomer call and no assertion that a second customer stays unchanged. The current code at src/domain/customers.js:49 is correct, so this is a test gap and not a live defect.

watchList.what_breaks: window.localStorage is read at module top level with no try around it. If the browser blocks site data and the getter throws a SecurityError, the module stops before load() and render() run. The page stays blank and shows no banner.
watchList.evidence: app.js:5 is `const store = createStore(window.localStorage);` with no try. store.js wraps only getItem.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether the getter throws depends on the browser and its settings. The guard does not allow a browser run in this session.
watchList.how_to_settle: In Chrome, block all site data for localhost, serve with python3 -m http.server 8000, open http://localhost:8000, and check whether the banner shows or main is blank with a SecurityError in the console.

watchList.what_breaks: crypto.randomUUID exists only in secure contexts. Served over plain http on a LAN IP, newId would throw inside the submit handlers, and Add customer, New order and Add line would fail with no message on the page.
watchList.evidence: app.js:22 has `newId: () => crypto.randomUUID()`, called unguarded from the view submit handlers. The documented run path (AGENTS.md: http://localhost:8000) is a secure context, where the call works.
watchList.why_unproven: This needs a browser on a non-localhost http origin, which is outside the documented run path and was not run here.
watchList.how_to_settle: Serve with python3 -m http.server 8000, open http://<LAN-IP>:8000, add a customer, and watch the page and the console for a TypeError.
